skill.name: shape
skill.description: Plan the UX and UI for a feature before writing code. Runs a structured discovery interview, then produces a design brief that guides implementation. Use during the planning phase to establish design direction, constraints, and strategy before any code is written.
skill.summary: Guides UX discovery and produces a design brief before implementation begins.
skill.author: pbakaus

content.value_statement: Teams often build interfaces before clarifying user goals, states, and constraints. This skill guides discovery and produces a design brief for implementation.
actual_capabilities: Runs a staged discovery interview before design decisions are made.
Captures users, goals, success criteria, content ranges, constraints, states, and anti-goals.
Produces a structured brief with feature summary, primary action, design direction, layout strategy, states, and interactions.
Identifies content requirements, recommended reference files, and open questions for implementation.
Asks for explicit confirmation and revises the brief when the user disagrees.
limitations: Requires design context from /impeccable and may require /impeccable teach first.
Depends on user answers for product goals, data ranges, and constraints.
Does not replace visual mockups, usability testing, or engineering estimates.

use_cases.title: Shape a New Product Feature
use_cases.description: Clarify audience, goals, edge cases, and success criteria before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Turn Ambiguous Requests Into Briefs
use_cases.description: Convert a broad UI request into a practical design plan with states and interaction guidance.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Design Handoff
use_cases.description: Create a concise brief that aligns visual direction, layout strategy, content needs, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for early UX planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use shape to plan a profile settings page for a small team app. Ask discovery questions before creating the brief.

prompt_templates.title: Define States and Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with known data concerns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use shape to plan a notification center. Focus on empty, loading, error, high-volume, and first-time states.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Implementation Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use shape to create a design brief for a billing dashboard. Include layout strategy, interactions, content requirements, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Shape a Complex Redesign
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with constraints and existing patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use shape to plan a mobile-first redesign of a project overview page. Account for existing patterns, localization, performance, and accessibility.

output_examples.input: Plan a filter panel for a reporting dashboard.
output: Feature summary explaining who uses the panel and what decisions it supports.
Primary action focused on narrowing reports quickly without losing context.
Key states covering no filters, many filters, saved filters, errors, and mobile use.
Open questions about default filters, permissions, and export behavior.

output_examples.input: Shape an onboarding checklist for a collaboration tool.
output: Design direction that feels calm, progress-oriented, and lightweight.
Layout strategy that emphasizes the next best action and completed milestones.
Interaction model for completing, skipping, and returning to checklist items.
Content requirements for labels, progress text, empty states, and success messages.

output_examples.input: Create a brief for a mobile account security screen.
output: Primary user action focused on understanding account risk and taking one security step.
States for secure, warning, critical issue, loading, and failed verification cases.
Accessibility notes for clear status language, touch targets, and non-color indicators.

best_practices: Use the skill before implementation decisions are made.
Provide concrete user roles, data ranges, constraints, and examples when possible.
Review and confirm the brief before handing it to an implementation workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to write production code directly.
Do not skip discovery and request a finished layout immediately.
Do not use it without project design context when that context is required.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a structured design brief for a feature before implementation starts.

faq.question: Does it write code?
faq.answer: No. It plans UX and UI direction, then prepares guidance for later implementation.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it during planning, before layout, component, and interaction decisions are locked.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the feature goal, target users, constraints, data ranges, examples, and known anti-goals.

faq.question: How does it use project design context?
faq.answer: It references existing /impeccable context and asks for setup when that context is missing.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
